Hi everyone.

Like a lot of people here, I'd been a lurker for most of my internet browsing experience in general. I had accounts with both Digg and Reddit, but lurked around besides digging/burying/upvoting/downvoting. It was easy, safe participation that gave me the slight right to call myself a part of those communities. And when those communities crumbled, I was upset, just like many others.

I do think (ex)Diggers/Redditors have the right to be upset about large fundamental changes to their online communities. It annoys me when people say "calm down, go outside, it's just a website." The world is becoming more centered around the internet, which means that yes, people might spend more time indoors on these websites. We call them public forums, and in many ways they have replaced the public square. (It makes avoiding panhandlers and street preachers easy enough, if thats what you want). But it wasn't even just that, because Digg and Reddit connected us to the rest of the WORLD, with an initial commitment to free speech. It helped us lurkers-at-heart connect with people about the random shit we were interested in. With both Reddit and Digg, the level, open playing field was compromised.

With Digg I was really pissed off. It was the first online community I really felt a part of (way better than Myspace, which was popular with my age group at the time). So it sucked to see it get compromised for profit and powerusers. When I left, I tried Reddit, hated the layout, gave up for a few weeks, and eventually caved. Like everyone else, it just took me a while to let the ugly layout fade into the background and let the content shine. Plus, it felt like the "truer" club, since I always saw people complaining about Digg just reposting from Reddit. And as great as 4chan/8chan can be... I've tried, but I just can't do the layout and format. Still love the idea though.

So now Reddit is gone. I was on it for longer than I was on Digg, and had honed my browsing experience to be the perfect combination of news, discussion, random, and silly. The first and biggest blow to my love of Reddit was the banning of those 5 "harassment" subs. It wasn't enough to keep me from Reddit, but after an onslaught of small chops at the last connecting threads (Victoria being let go and the shitty behavior of admins, Pao, and others, the god-awful apology, etc.), I decided to commit to Voat.

Thankfully, it's not difficult in the slightest. The layout is so similar but so much cleaner, the community is much smaller and thus alleviates a lot of the problems from bloated Reddit, and there are restrictions on voating. It might seem lame to expect to grieve over losing a website, I don't know what else to call it, but I actually barely had to with Reddit, unlike Digg. The people here on Voat represent the basis of the community I love, the one that loves free speech, even when it's uncomfortable or infuriating, and the potential that the internet has to further that ideal. It doesn't seem like Voat will go down the toilet anytime soon, but if it does, we'll always find a way.

I just have to come to terms with committing to contributing. Even writing this, I'm anxious about people I don't know rolling their eyes, but fuck it. Thanks for reading this far, and let me know your experience and if you agree or disagree or whatever oh god what have I done
